Technology stocks were falling Thursday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing over 1.0% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 1.2% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Pareteum Corp. ( TEUM ) was edging higher Thursday afternoon, rising just under 0.5%, after the cloud communication services company said it has agreed to acquire Artilium, an UK-based enterprise software firm, for $105 million in cash and stock. Under the terms of the proposed transaction, acquisition, Artilium investors will receive 0.1016 of a Pareteum share plus GBP0.019 in cash for each Artilium share they own. The company is expecting the deal willl significantly increase its non-GAAP FY19 per-share earnings and also producing strong growth in its pro-forma operating cashflow generation while providing material cost and revenue synergies.
In other sector news:
- Twitter ( TWTR ) fell over 3% in recent Thursday trading after the micro-blogging platform priced a $1 billion private placement of 0.25% convertible senior notes due 2024. Initial buyers also received a 30-day option to buy up to $150 million more of the notes. The notes have an initial conversion price of $57.14 a share and can be converted into common stock at the owner's option through March 2024. The company expects to use $70.6 million of the net proceeds to fund a convertible note hedge transaction protecting investors from dilution if the notes are converted into stock.
- Comtech Telecommunications ( CMTL ) slumped almost 6% on Thursday after the networking equipment company projected per-share earnings for its current Q4 ending July 31 trailing Wall Street forecasts, expecting between $0.24 to $0.30 per share compared with the Capital IQ consensus expecting $0.45 per share. Comtech also earned $0.34 per share during the three months ended April 30, up from $0.19 per share during the same quarter last year and exceeding the Capital IQ consensus by $0.22 per share. Net sales rose to $147.9 million from $127.8 million during the prior year and topped the $145.4 million analyst mean. Comtech also raised the bottom end of its Q4 earnings outlook by $0.09 per share to a new range of $1.17 to $1.23 per share to top the Street view by at least $0.01 per share.
